title: The open knots are twisted Fibonacci knots
claim: The six non-symmetric knots excluding three tuples form one orbit under place permutations and complement, and each is the Fibonacci knot with one or two negated places (S(x, y, z) = Fib(x, y, not z)); so native networks of such a knot with pins are Fibonacci networks with twisted (disequality) edges and complemented pins. In the Fibonacci eigenbasis a twist is the reflection [[2 phi, phi], [phi, -2 phi]]/D^2 with one negative entry, so the count is a signed two-spin sum. McQuillan's winding fails because the knot is not windable, the Fibonacci holographic algorithm fails because a twist is not diagonal, and weighted Fibonacci gates admit edge activities but not twists.
failure_conditions: The six knots do not form one orbit, or one of them is not a Fibonacci knot with negated legs.
A random network whose count differs from that of its twisted Fibonacci network or from the signed two-spin sum.
foundation_claim_scope: Finite relations and random finite networks; known algorithms cited as background. No P versus NP claim.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py (standard library) confirms the orbit and the twists by enumeration, and the agreement of direct counts, twisted Fibonacci counts and the signed two-spin sum on 1,000 random networks; three controls. Cited algorithms are background. No human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with finite checks
